back: Adding more units of a variable input to a fixed input eventually gives smaller extra output per unit.
AP = total product ÷ units of variable input.
MP = change in total product ÷ change in input.
I: MP rising (increasing returns). II: MP falling but positive (best level here). III: MP negative, TP falling (never).

front: Most profitable level of an input
back: Keep adding while MP × output price > cost of the extra unit; stop where they are about equal.

front: Effect of input and output prices
back: Dearer input or cheaper output: use less. Cheaper input or dearer output: use more.
Fertiliser, feed, labour, seed rate, water and chemicals all have a most profitable level below the maximum-yield level.
